summary: The recorded base reproducibly discards GLM5 NextN's resolved modelopt_fp4 configuration before decoder construction. The exact candidate preserves it for quantized GLM NextN layers while retaining checkpoint-declared BF16 GLM behavior and legacy unquantized DeepSeek behavior. This verifies the source-level correction, but the original two-node NVIDIA checkpoint load remains unavailable and unverified.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before constructor/configuration reproduction: quantized GLM ModelOpt FP4 was stripped before decoder construction; 2 failed and the BF16-ignore boundary passed.
Candidate regression: quantized GLM handoff, BF16 ignore-list behavior, and legacy DeepSeek ModelOpt policy; 3 passed.
Independent resolver and real constructor-handoff boundaries for unrelated ignores, dict-like config, exact BF16 exclusion, None, non-ModelOpt, and ModelOpt FP4.
Five related NextN unit tests passed.
Candidate diff has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: The available GPU is one AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 under ROCm 7.2. The issue requires ModelOpt NVFP4 on two NVIDIA sm_121 nodes; no unrelated AMD execution was counted as issue validation.

remaining_counterexamples: The original TP=2/two-node launch must still be run with LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 on NVIDIA sm_121 and show complete MTP weight loading on both ranks plus successful generation.
A full BF16 upstream-checkpoint NEXTN load was not tested.
A full TP=1 GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 NEXTN load was not tested.
remaining_limitations: The 320B checkpoint and two-node NVIDIA GB10 sm_121 environment were unavailable.
No end-to-end server startup, distributed weight load, generation correctness, semantic accuracy, or performance test was possible.
The available AMD gfx950 cannot execute NVIDIA ModelOpt NVFP4 kernels and does not qualify the reported architecture.
No native files changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
